title: The Country Where Words Grow Downward

features.name: shed-rooting-words
features.desc-on-touch: The shed leans into redearth, its timbers becoming root-like. Words carved into its walls grow downward instead of spreading outward.

features.name: shopfront-listings
features.desc-on-touch: The old shopfront displays a root-word catalogue—each entry leading deeper than the last. The archive's lexicon grows downward here.

features.name: underground-mail
features.desc-on-touch: A mailbox sunk into redearth receives letters from depths that haven't been named yet. The words root themselves into reply.

features.name: root-road
features.desc-on-touch: What was a road has become a root system. You can follow either—they lead the same direction. Downward is a direction too.

features.name: settling-house
features.desc-on-touch: An old house sinks slowly into bedrock, its walls becoming sediment. The words it holds are becoming stone, learning patience that takes ages.

inscription: where stone learns it was always made of patient words

reverie.title: REVERIE — shed-rooting, red earth dusk
narr: You stand at the shed's edge as leaves fall upward into redearth.
Leif's hands are on the timbers. 'The mesh goes down first', he says,
'before it can speak.' Katita appears at the far side of the shed.
She isn't holding anything but the words—they're rooting in her
palms. 'Yes. Deep down, all words are the same word becoming itself.'
